```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 6, fig.height = 4)
library(mlvtoolbox)
```

A drawing contains ordered segment matrices in image coordinates. Keep
individual contours separate: contour identity affects junction counts,
curvature and stimulus selection.

```{r drawing}
drawing <- mlv_drawing(
  list(matrix(c(5, 5, 35, 5), 1),
       matrix(c(20, 2, 20, 25), 1),
       rbind(c(5, 15, 10, 20), c(10, 20, 15, 15))),
  width = 40, height = 30
)
drawing <- compute_contour_properties(drawing)
as.data.frame(drawing)
drawing$junctions[, c("x", "y", "type", "min_angle")]
plot(drawing, property = "junctions")
```

Orientation is directed and measured in degrees. Orientation histograms are
axial (modulo 180) and length weighted. Curvature is a wrapped turning angle
divided by segment length, including an explicit last-segment convention.

```{r statistics}
stats <- contour_statistics(drawing, properties = c("orientation", "curvature"))
head(stats)
feature_table(drawing, properties = c("length", "curvature"), bins = 4)
```

Stimulus selection uses whole contours and conservative length budgets. Changes
to geometry invalidate derived tables so old properties cannot silently follow
a rotated or segmented drawing.

```{r manipulation}
parts <- split_contours(drawing, property = "length", fraction = 0.5)
sum(as.data.frame(parts$top)$length)
sum(as.data.frame(drawing)$length) * 0.5
plot(clip_circle(rotate_drawing(drawing, 25), radius = 12))
```

The medial-axis workflow first creates an ink mask, then computes signed
distance, average outward flux and a thinned skeleton. It records the exact
threshold and backend. Here TRUE denotes ink; image arrays index row, column.

```{r mat}
result <- analyse_mat(drawing, min_branch_points = 2)
result$mat
result$mat$parameters
plot(result$drawing, property = "parallelism")
head(contour_statistics(result$drawing, "parallelism"))
```

Valid zero ratings are retained. Unmapped pixels are NA and have a separate
mapping mask. Branch derivatives, smoothing, score exponents and tangent
mapping have explicit parameters.

The package uses exact Euclidean distances and the identified Octave-image
Pratt morphology backend. Small synthetic fixtures compare compiled kernels to
executed references and independent exhaustive calculations. This does not
establish MATLAB-specific morphology/raster equivalence or validity on every
class of natural image. Rasterization, graph tracing, axial mean orientation
and taper smoothing are documented method choices.

For file adapters, use read_mlv_svg(), read_mlv_mat(), and trace_contours().
Their dependencies are optional. SVG curves are sampled; unsupported visible
elements error by default. MAT v5 structures are supported. RGB extraction uses
an explicitly supplied trace_rgb() provider; model weights and preprocessing
remain the provider's responsibility.
